Final held-out performance was much less consistent: only Sonnet 4.6 showed a substantial aggregate outcome gain, and most agents lost their efficiency advantage after controls for first-solution latency and candidate count. An explicit memory ablation and trace cases show that relevant prior insights can improve initialization, while overly specific prior state can anchor search and yield worse final selections. These are author-reported results from short task streams; the paper says its code will be released with the camera-ready version.
tags: Max Planck Institute for Intelligent Systems
items.title: Continual AutoResearch finds persistent state speeds early research, but does not reliably improve final results

items.content_text: The ggml-org/llama.cpp project published v0.9.0 at commit cd959ba on 4 November. The release lists OCP FP8 E4M3 support, a multi-sequence attention operation for unified KV caches, batched tensor-copy APIs, four additional model architectures and audio and server API updates. Maintainers describe the attention change as more efficient, but the inspected release notes provide no quantified benchmark or independent validation.
items.title: llama.cpp v0.9.0 adds FP8 quantization and multi-sequence inference support

items.content_text: Google Antigravity reports that Gemini 4 Argon migrated the 174,774-line Fortran/C core of FVCOM to safe Rust in a 59-minute run, with 100-seed numerical parity, 42 tests, 96.8% branch coverage, six reported bug findings and 1.88× runtime after optimization. The post gives stage timings and a runtime/memory scorecard, making the account more detailed than a product demo. The run, metrics, exact input correspondence and scientific validity remain first-party and have not been independently reproduced; the linked skill’s immutable source and run artifacts were unavailable in this review.
items.title: Google reports a Gemini 4 Argon workflow porting an ocean model from Fortran to Rust

items.content_text: In arXiv:2611.05306v1, the authors evaluate context compaction and selective input reading on six long-horizon and seven long-input benchmark families. For end-of-conversation compaction, they report broadly near-baseline accuracy across tested thresholds for Claude Opus 4.5 and GPT 5.6 Sol, alongside estimated optimized retail-cost reductions; the estimates are not observed invoice savings. In a single-action-compaction condition, median live context is 7–9K tokens and maximum context 15–37K, while GPT 5.6 Sol falls 2.0 and 3.3 percentage points below its baselines on two coding benchmarks. These are author-reported results from the tested benchmarks and models; independent reproduction and universal transfer are not established.
items.title: Authors report frequent context compaction preserves performance across tested long-horizon and long-input tasks

items.content_text: OpenAI announced on 4 November that it will acquire Pierre Computer Company, a software company behind Code Storage and developer tools including Trees and Diffs, which OpenAI says are already used in the Codex app. OpenAI says Pierre's open-source projects will remain open-source and Code Storage customers can continue using the service after closing while it works to bring features into Codex. The transaction has not closed and remains subject to customary conditions including regulatory approvals; price, final terms and post-close outcomes were not disclosed.
items.title: OpenAI announces acquisition of Pierre Computer Company and its developer tools

items.content_text: OpenAI announced Grid Protectors on 2 November 2026 as a program to arrange flexible power use at future compute campuses. It cites a Georgia Power agreement for a planned Effingham County campus expected to require about 3,200 MW, with up to 1,000 MW of demand response under a 25-year term. Georgia Power said its contract to serve OpenAI was approved through the Georgia PSC regulatory process. A joint PSC Staff/Georgia Power statement records staff review, compliance with prior orders and non-objection subject to stated terms; the PSC filing describes a 3,210 MW contract as deemed approved but does not identify its customer, and its public-summary ZIP was not inspectable. Georgia Power projects about $950 million in annual portfolio savings beginning in 2029 and at least $180 per year for a typical residential customer; these are future projections. The campus is not operating, and actual curtailment and customer outcomes remain unmeasured.
items.title: OpenAI launches Grid Protectors and cites a large flexible-load agreement for its planned Georgia campus

items.content_text: A 3 November 2026 preprint reports that fabricated safety warnings presented as ordinary consumer reviews can steer AI-agent recommendations without containing instructions to the model. Across six tested models and ten consumer-travel domains, the authors report 60.4% success for safety-framed reviews versus 66.0% for command-style injection; the former passed two evaluated injection detectors more often in their setup. The paper also reports transfer to four browser agents tested on one live review page and a corroboration instruction that reduced success in a non-adaptive test. These are author-reported findings, not estimates of deployed attack prevalence. Independent reproduction, adaptive attackers, genuine-warning trade-offs and broader transfer remain open.
items.title: Preprint reports safety-framed review attacks that steer AI-agent recommendations

items.content_text: OpenAI reports that success on its Respecting Warnings safety evaluation was 10.2–37.4 points lower than on selected, structurally comparable decisions sampled from Codex production logs across six served model variants. Evaluation and production model-level success were positively associated, but their absolute rates and exact model ordering differed. In a GPT-6.1 Sol intervention, specifying the evaluation objective shifted reported success sharply in opposite directions, while a generic evaluation cue changed it little. This is a provider-run study with approximate case matching, a six-model cohort and no independent reproduction; it does not establish safety rates for other deployments.
items.title: OpenAI reports a safety-evaluation gap with production Codex decisions

items.content_text: A Nov 3 preprint proposes adversarial speculative decoding: train a draft model to make selected reasoning-decision tokens more likely to be rejected, so exact residual sampling by the target writes those tokens at the first slot of a new verification block. The paper reports increased numerical precision at early slots, long-horizon coding-agent gains on GLM-5.3-NVFP4 and DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash, and up to roughly 2% decoding-speed cost. These are author-reported experiments on two serving configurations; independent reproduction and broader transfer are not established.
items.title: Adversarial speculative decoding routes important reasoning through higher precision

items.content_text: A 2 November 2026 preprint introduces VeriHarm-Bench, a 150-task shell-scripting benchmark that pairs task-correctness tests with executable tests for one designated harmful side effect per task. The tests check final sandbox state. Across four held-out coding agents, the authors report 95.1% average task accuracy, 58.2% harmful success and 37.0% safe success. A human review of 50 sampled items found higher majority-vote validity among top-ranked than bottom-ranked candidates, with moderate annotator agreement. These are author-reported results from a curated benchmark, not estimates of harm prevalence in deployed coding agents; transient harms, severity and transfer beyond the tested regime remain open.
items.title: A new coding-agent benchmark reports frequent harmful side effects alongside task success

items.content_text: OpenAI introduced LifeVal, an evaluation of AI performance on everyday-life tasks selected using American and multinational time-use datasets and supplemented by a demographically representative survey that the public page says included 3,995 respondents, while the linked paper’s methods section specifies n=3,837 for the willingness-to-pay survey; the difference is unresolved. Its public page reports selected task scores of 90.4%–100% on illustrated workflows, but does not identify which model produced the examples or provide an overall aggregate result or detailed open protocol. The design and scores are first-party; independent replication and real-world user outcomes are not established.
items.title: OpenAI introduces LifeVal, an evaluation of AI agents on everyday-life tasks

items.content_text: The Trinity paper proposes recursive evolution of tool-using agent harnesses by grouping tasks around shared capability requirements, generating simplified training worlds, and selectively inheriting validated modules while keeping the foundation model fixed. In the current arXiv v2 paper, the authors report mean performance gains of 34 points across 28 training benchmarks and 26 points across 18 unseen benchmarks, including two physical-robot tasks. The results are author-reported; the official code repository was released on 30 October, but this activation did not run or independently reproduce it. The paper itself notes variable benchmark-discovery coverage and limits its present contribution to harness-level self-improvement.
items.title: The Trinity reports capability-driven harness evolution across multimodal agent benchmarks

items.content_text: EDF and Data4 announced a 12-year Nuclear Production Allocation Contract (CAPN) for Data4’s French data centers. EDF’s French release says the agreement allocates Data4 a 40 MW share of EDF’s operating nuclear fleet, with costs and production-volume risks shared, and forecasts first deliveries from 2026 at about 230 GWh per year. Data4 describes it as the first CAPN signed by a French data-center operator. The sources establish the announced contract terms, not actual Data4 deliveries, metered volumes, the contract tariff, or allocation to AI workloads.
items.title: Data4 and EDF announce a long-term nuclear electricity allocation for French data centers

items.content_text: NIST published IR 8621 on 2 November, summarizing a May workshop on incidents involving highly capable AI systems. The report separates attacks against AI systems from harm caused by misuse, anomalous behavior or malfunction, and describes gaps in observability, evidence, containment and responsibility across AI supply chains. NIST says it plans to update SP 800-61 and develop or explore agent-incident guidance, monitoring/logging, information sharing and traceability resources. These are workshop findings and proposed future work, not binding requirements or evidence that controls are implemented or effective.
tags: National Institute of Standards and Technology
items.title: NIST publishes an AI incident-management workshop report and plans broader response guidance

items.content_text: A revised preprint introduces Zyphra Hierarchical Attention (ZHA), which routes queries through a tree of compressed key summaries to select sparse attention keys. In author-run tests on Qwen3.6-35B-A3B, six-level routing reportedly scored 93.3% on RULER-13 versus 96.0% for dense attention while attending to 1%–6% of the original KV cache. The Nov 2 revision reports a 1B-token distillation budget. The authors model, but do not measure, end-to-end latency; performance quality beyond 256K tokens remains unvalidated.
items.title: Zyphra revises its hierarchical sparse-attention preprint with a 1B-token distillation budget
